question: In paediatric hypovolaemic shock, hypotension is typically an early and reliable sign that should trigger fluid resuscitation, appearing before tachycardia and prolonged capillary refill.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Hypotension is a late, decompensated sign in paediatric shock. Children compensate remarkably well through tachycardia and peripheral vasoconstriction, maintaining blood pressure until approximately 25–30% of circulating volume is lost. Early recognition relies on tachycardia, prolonged CRT, and altered mental status — not a fall in blood pressure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is FALSE. In children, hypotension is a LATE sign of shock, appearing only after compensatory mechanisms (tachycardia, vasoconstriction, increased cardiac contractility) are overwhelmed. A child can lose up to 25–30% of circulating volume while maintaining blood pressure. Tachycardia and prolonged capillary refill time are the EARLY clinical markers that should trigger fluid resuscitation.
